pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we express the quantity or amount of something?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts
2. use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes to a partner. (skill: use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts.
3. Practise this skill: use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we express the quantity or amount of something?
2. Why should we give the exact amount of something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts.
5. Be able to: use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
